preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (deployer)
Attacker must hold some MSA tokens to demonstrate the exploit
swapAndLiquifyEnabled should be true (default is false, but owner can enable it)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, first enable swapAndLiquifyEnabled via setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(true). Then set _taxFee and _liquidityFee to high values (e.g., 49 each) using setTaxFeePercent(49) and setLiquidityFeePercent(49). Transfer MSA tokens to another address (non-excluded from fees) to trigger the high fee mechanism. The contract will accumulate fees and eventually swap them for BNB, which can be drained to the marketing address (controlled by owner). Alternatively, set marketingAddress to attacker's address first via setMarketingAddress().

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract owner has excessive privileges to set fee percentages up to 100% (though limited by UI constraints). By setting high taxFee and liquidityFee, any token transfer (except to/from excluded addresses) will incur massive fees. These fees accumulate in the contract and when swapAndLiquify is enabled and threshold is met, tokens are swapped to BNB and sent to marketingAddress. The owner can set marketingAddress to their own address and drain the accumulated BNB.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank. 2. Set marketingAddress to attacker address. 3. Enable swapAndLiquify. 4. Set high taxFee and liquidityFee (e.g., 49 each). 5. Transfer tokens from a non-excluded address to trigger fee accumulation. 6. Wait for fees to accumulate above minimumTokensBeforeSwap threshold. 7. Trigger swap manually or wait for auto-swap. 8. Profit from BNB sent to marketingAddress (attacker).
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Start prank as owner. 2. Call setMarketingAddress(attacker). 3. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(true). 4. Call setTaxFeePercent(49) and setLiquidityFeePercent(49). 5. Create a victim address (not excluded from fees). 6. Transfer some MSA tokens to victim. 7. Have victim transfer tokens to another address to incur high fees. 8. Fees accumulate in contract. 9. If needed, manually trigger swap by calling transfer on contract to push over threshold. 10. Marketing address (attacker) receives BNB.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract accumulates fees in its own balance when transfers occur. When swapAndLiquify is enabled and the contract balance exceeds minimumTokensBeforeSwap, it swaps tokens for BNB and sends a portion to marketingAddress. The owner can set marketingAddress to their address and set high fees to extract value.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Use more moderate fees to ensure transfers succeed. 2. Make multiple smaller transfers to accumulate fees gradually. 3. Ensure the contract accumulates enough tokens to trigger swap. 4. Set marketingAddress to attacker. 5. Trigger swap by making a transfer that pushes contract balance over threshold.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner. 2. Set marketingAddress to attacker. 3. Enable swapAndLiquify. 4. Set moderate fees (e.g., 20% each). 5. Set low swap threshold. 6. Transfer tokens from owner to multiple victims. 7. Have victims make transfers to accumulate fees in contract. 8. Trigger swap by making final transfer. 9. Attacker receives BNB.
attempts.failure_reflection: The error occurred during the swap process when the router tried to transfer tokens from the contract. This suggests either: 1) The contract doesn't have enough token balance from fees, 2) The allowance isn't properly set, or 3) The swap is being triggered with insufficient tokens. The issue is likely that we're setting fees too high (98% total) which might leave the victim with insufficient balance to complete the transfer after fees.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The owner has complete control over fee distribution percentages. By setting liquidityPercent = 0 and marketingPercent = 100 (or high value), when swaps happen, all BNB goes to marketingAddress. Combined with setting marketingAddress to attacker and enabling high fees, this allows the owner to extract value.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner. 2. Set marketingAddress to attacker. 3. Enable swapAndLiquify. 4. Set fees to moderate levels. 5. Use changePercentage to set liquidityPercent = 0, marketingPercent = 100. 6. Make transfers to accumulate fees. 7. Trigger swap.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner address. 2. Start prank as owner. 3. Set marketingAddress to attacker. 4. Enable swapAndLiquify. 5. Set taxFee and liquidityFee to 10% each. 6. Use changePercentage(0, 0, 100) to send all BNB to marketing. 7. Set low swap threshold. 8. Transfer tokens to victims. 9. Have victims make transfers to accumulate fees. 10. Trigger swap.
attempts.failure_reflection: The error persists because the reflection token mechanics are complex. The contract's internal accounting (rOwned vs tOwned) might be causing issues with the swap. Instead of trying to trigger the complex swap mechanism, we should use a simpler owner privilege: set marketingPercent to 100% and liquidityPercent to 0% so all fees go to marketing address when swap happens.
